leftEvidence.title: Achish places David beside a Philistine campaign

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Achish tells David he will go with him to battle, and David answers in language that leaves his action unstated while receiving appointment as bodyguard.
points.right: The commanders question the Hebrews in the ranks, recall David’s song, reject Achish’s defense, and compel David to return at dawn.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places David stands on the brink of war against Israel inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places David is removed from the battle without the text stating what he would have done inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Samuel 28:1–2 and 1 Samuel 29:1–11 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Philistine Brink and Recovery” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.
payload.tension: 1 Samuel 28:1–2 foregrounds David stands on the brink of war against Israel; 1 Samuel 29:1–11 foregrounds David is removed from the battle without the text stating what he would have done. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
